width.$description: The standard hairline width used throughout the system.

style.$description: The standard border style. Solid everywhere; dashed and dotted borders are not part of the visual language.

instant.$description: Zero duration. Use to disable a transition explicitly rather than omitting the property.

fast.$description: Fast — hover and other immediate feedback.

normal.$description: The default duration for most state changes.

slow.$description: Slow, for movements large enough that the eye needs to track them.

slower.$description: Slowest. Reserve for entrances of large surfaces; anything routine at this speed feels sluggish.

linear.$description: Constant speed. Correct for continuous motion such as a spinner, wrong for anything that starts and stops.

in.$description: Accelerating. For elements leaving the screen.

out.$description: Decelerating. For elements entering — they arrive rather than stop.
Symmetric. For elements that move from one place to another and stay on screen throughout.

spring.$description: Overshoots slightly before settling, giving movement a sense of weight.

primary.$description: Default text colour. Use for body copy and anything the reader is meant to actually read.

secondary.$description: Supporting text that sits alongside primary content — helper text, metadata, timestamps. Still fully legible, just lower in the hierarchy.

tertiary.$description: Third-level text. Use sparingly; if three levels of text hierarchy are not clearly distinguishable in context, the layout is doing too much.

subtle.$description: The quietest readable text. Placeholder-adjacent content such as counts, units, and inline hints.

disabled.$description: Text in a disabled control. Deliberately fails normal contrast expectations to signal non-interactivity — never use it for content the user needs to read.

inverse.$description: Text on a dark or saturated surface, such as a primary button or brand banner.

brand.$description: Text that carries brand identity — a link, a brand wordmark, an active nav label. Not for body copy.

error.$description: Text Error. Semantic role — reference this rather than the value beneath it.

success.$description: Text Success. Semantic role — reference this rather than the value beneath it.

primary.$description: The base canvas. Most of the interface sits on this.

secondary.$description: A raised or grouped surface — cards, panels, the assistant's message bubble. Warm off-white rather than grey, so it reads as a surface rather than a shadow.

tertiary.$description: The third surface level, for nested groupings and inset areas. Rarely needed; reach for spacing or a border before a third fill.

brand.$description: The single accent fill. Reserved for the one primary action in a view and for active states — its scarcity is what makes it read as important.

hover.$description: Hover wash for otherwise unfilled interactive rows and menu items. Tinted toward the brand hue so hover feels connected to the accent rather than a generic grey.

inverse.$description: Background Inverse. Semantic role — reference this rather than the value beneath it.

dark.$description: The pressed and hovered form of the brand fill. Darker rather than lighter, so the control appears to recede under the cursor.

default.$description: The standard hairline between regions. Should be visible without being the first thing the eye lands on.

active.$description: Border for a focused or selected control. Carries the brand hue so focus is unmistakably intentional.

disabled.$description: Border on a disabled control. Lower contrast than default, matching the muted fill it accompanies.

brand.$description: Brand-coloured border for outlined controls that need brand emphasis without a brand fill.

success.$description: Border on a success surface. Never the only signal — pair with an icon and text.

info.$description: Border on an informational surface. Never the only signal — pair with an icon and text.

error.$description: Border on an error surface or invalid field. Never the only signal — pair with an icon and an actionable message.

warning.$description: Border on a warning surface. Never the only signal — pair with an icon and text.

subtle.$description: Border Subtle. Semantic role — reference this rather than the value beneath it.

primary.$description: Default icon colour. Slightly lighter than primary text, because icon strokes read heavier than glyphs at the same value.

secondary.$description: Supporting icons — decorative affordances, inactive toolbar items.

disabled.$description: Icon in a disabled control.

brand.$description: Icon carrying brand emphasis, such as an active nav item or a brand-marked action.

fg.$description: Text and icon colour on a success surface. Dark enough to meet contrast against the matching background token.

bg.$description: Background for a success message. Pale enough that foreground text remains the dominant element.

border.$description: Border for a success surface, mid-ramp so it separates the surface without competing with its text.

stroke.$description: Feedback Success Stroke. Semantic role — reference this rather than the value beneath it.

bg.$description: Background for a warning — something that needs attention but is not yet a failure.

sm.$description: Internal padding for standard controls such as inputs and buttons.

md.$description: Internal padding for containers — cards, dialogs, panels.

xs.$description: Sharpest radius. For small elements where a larger curve would look bulbous — checkboxes, tight tags.

md.$description: The default radius. Buttons, inputs, and most controls use this.

lg.$description: Larger radius for containers — cards, panels, popovers.

xl.$description: Softest rectangular radius, for large surfaces such as modals.

full.$description: Fully round. Pills, avatars, toggle thumbs. A large constant rather than 50%, so it stays a pill on any aspect ratio.

1.$description: Barely-there lift. Hover on an otherwise flat card.

2.$description: Resting elevation for cards and raised surfaces.

3.$description: Dropdowns, popovers, and menus — floating above content but anchored to a trigger.

4.$description: High elevation for detached floating surfaces.

5.$description: Maximum elevation, for modals and sheets that sit above a scrim.

none.$description: No shadow. An explicit token rather than omitting the property, so a component can flatten a surface that would otherwise inherit elevation.

md.$description: Alias of elevation-3, kept for components that describe elevation by size rather than by level.

color.$description: Focus ring colour. Carries the brand hue so focus reads as deliberate rather than as an error.

offset.$description: Gap between the control and its focus ring, so the ring stays legible against the control's own border.

width.$description: Thickness of the focus ring. Wide enough to be unmissable at a glance, which is the entire job of a focus indicator.

ring.$description: The complete focus indicator. Applied on focus-visible so it appears for keyboard users without following the mouse.

default.$description: Standard easing. Decelerating, so movement arrives gently rather than stopping dead.

fade.$description: Symmetric easing for opacity changes, where there is no sense of physical arrival to soften.

spring.$description: Slight overshoot, for elements that should feel physical — a toggle thumb, a drawer catching.

fast.$description: Quick transition for immediate feedback such as hover. Fast enough to feel instant while still smoothing the change.

normal.$description: The default transition. Use unless there is a reason not to.

slow.$description: Deliberate transition for larger movements — a panel opening, a layout shift the user should be able to follow.

fade.$description: Transition for opacity-only changes, paired with the fade easing curve.

spring.$description: Transition with overshoot, for controls that benefit from feeling physical.
